doc.title: George Wein interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Swing was the current music
summary: Wein explains that their repertoire of Dorsey, Miller and Goodman was the hip music of the day, before bebop.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Isn’t that interesting. You know I have to remind myself, when you talk about some of those tunes you were playing with your first band, they sound old but for you guys, that was the current music of the day, is that right?

Oh yes. We were not playing old music. Old music was Bix Beiderbecke. We were playing Teddy Wilson, Benny Goodman, it was swing. That was the hip music of the day, before bebop. It was before the war and we were trying to be — you know, Duke Ellington. But I was getting into it. © Fiillius Jazz Archive -4-
